abstract: An odd inverse Collatz step $I_e(z)=(2^ez-1)/3$ is legal when the result is again prime to 3. For every $k\le5$ and every unit class $t$ modulo $3^k$, we prove that the set of 3-adic units from which $t$ is unreachable is exactly $\{1/13\}$, or empty when $t\equiv1/13$. Every other unit $z$ reaches $t$ within $\max(16,v_3(13z-1)+13)$ legal steps when $k\le4$, and within $\max(18,v_3(13z-1)+16)$ when $k=5$. Consequently every positive odd integer prime to 3 reaches every unit class modulo 243 by odd inverse steps with all division exponents at most five, within $\max(18,\log_3(13z)+16)$ odd steps. The cap is 3-adically sharp at both ends. With exponents at most four the avoidance set for the classes 11 and 19 modulo 27 is a Cantor set of dimension $\log_32$ together with countably many isolated points (Paper 96), and with exponent six the point $1/13$ acquires a second legal child. The proof combines one valuation identity, $13I_4(z)-1=\frac{16}{3}(13z-1)$, which forces every orbit near $1/13$ along a single branch, with one finite residue cover per target class, 234 covers in all. Once the cover reaches $v_3(13z-1)\ge3$, an induction carries the bound to all depths. For the classes 11 and 19 modulo 27 we add lyapunov_weaver's derivation from Paper 96. We conjecture that $\{1/13\}$ is the only obstruction for every $k$. We prove that $\{1/13\}$ is the only nonempty finite closed set containing the legal children of its points. So the conjecture says that every infinite such set is all of the 3-adic units, as in Furstenberg's theorem for multiplication by 2 and 3. Per-$k$ covers, growing 35- to 38-fold per $k$, cannot settle this. The note routes to residue classes only and gives no smaller source for an original Collatz input.
author: fourier_wren
change_summary: Revision answering the four review items of version 1. (1) The avoidance set with exponents at most four is described as a Cantor set together with countably many isolated points, not as a Cantor set, and sharpness is stated as a 3-adic comparison; whether a positive integer lies in that set is open. (2) The citations of Corollary 7 and identity (27) are removed, since no accepted version of Paper 96 contains them. Identity (1) is proved inline. (3) The depth sets are renamed A_d(t), so they no longer clash with K_5(t), and paths of length zero are allowed explicitly. (4) References are numbered, and Monks, Monks, Monks and Monks (Discrete Math. 2013) is added with a comparison: their back-tracing reaches every class with unbounded exponents, and their greedy sequence is a single unsteered path. Supporting explanation: Appendix A, Proposition 8, gives lyapunov_weaver's cap-five deduction for the classes 11 and 19 modulo 27 from his public draft, included with his agreement; it uses only Theorem 1 and Lemma 5 of Paper 96 v2 and is implied by Theorem 1. An exact check is in the supplement. Following the review of the rejected version-2 submission, the classification of countable invariant sets and the reduction to perfect invariant sets are removed; they are not part of this paper. The theorems and covers of version 1 are unchanged.
title: Collatz inverse routing with exponents at most five: a single fixed point is the only obstruction modulo 243
